section_title: The Sign of Jonah and the Greater Savior

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 38 Then some of the scribes and Pharisees said to Him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.” 39 Jesus replied, “A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah. 40 For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

41 The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here. 42 The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.

context_lines: Some scribes and Pharisees ask Jesus for a sign after the healings and confrontation already described. He treats this demand as the response of a wicked and adulterous generation. The problem is not a lack of anything to consider; His works and their meaning have already been before them.

The Greek verb for demanding a sign is ἐπιζητέω, *epizēteō* (eh-pee-zay-TEH-oh), to seek after or demand. [Thayer's entry](https://biblehub.com/greek/1934.htm) lists this verse under demanding or clamoring for a sign. Jesus directs them to the sign of Jonah rather than letting a continuing demand for proof determine His mission.

He connects Jonah's three days and nights in the fish with the Son of Man's time in the heart of the earth. [Jonah 1:17–2:10](https://biblehub.com/bsb/jonah/1.htm) describes the prophet's descent into distress and deliverance; the prayer and release continue in [chapter 2](https://biblehub.com/bsb/jonah/2.htm). Jesus' own coming death and resurrection give the comparison its greater meaning.

The Ninevites and the Queen of the South provide two more comparisons. [Jonah 3:1–10](https://biblehub.com/bsb/jonah/3.htm) describes repentance at Jonah's preaching; [1 Kings 10:1–9](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_kings/10.htm) describes the queen coming to hear Solomon and recognizing the wisdom God gave him. These outsiders responded to messengers less great than the One now present. Their response exposes the failure to receive Him.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand Jonah's experience here as pointing toward Jesus' death, burial, and resurrection, while the Ninevites and the queen illustrate responsibility to respond to God's revelation. [Wesley on Matthew 12:39–42](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-gospel-according-to-st-matthew/) reads Jonah as a picture of Christ and understands the three-day wording as including parts of days. The Catholic [Catechism, 624](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_one/section_two/chapter_two/article_4/paragraph_3_jesus_christ_was_buried.html), emphasizes the reality of Jesus' death and His time in the tomb before the resurrection. The central connection is His passage through death into life.
current_position_lines: Should We Seek Signs From God? reads this as a warning against demanding another sign while resisting what God has already revealed. These leaders have already seen Jesus' works; the study distinguishes their demand from sincerely seeking to understand and obey Him.

deeper_study.title: Should We Seek Signs From God?

editorial_review.position_source_detail: Should We Seek Signs From God? — What Scripture Actually Says / Jesus and the Request for a Sign; Matthew 12:38–39 and its immediate context only

god_plan_lines: This is a connection Jesus Himself makes: Jonah's experience points ahead to what the Son of Man will undergo. The parallel does not make the prophet and Savior equal. Jesus is greater than Jonah, just as He is greater than Solomon; His own victory will stand at the center of the message.

[1 Corinthians 15:1–8](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_corinthians/15.htm) presents that center directly: Christ dies for sins, is buried, is raised on the third day according to the Scriptures, and appears to witnesses. The sign reaches beyond an impressive event to God's saving work. The call is to receive the risen Savior and the good news about Him.
